messages.subject: HMM AR1
parts:
Hi

I am trying to build a HMM AR(1) model with potentially more than 2 states. I am struggling with the `state` matrix. Every t-th row should be a simplex. I am obviously doing something wrong with the indexing of `state`.

It would also be nice to keep kk[T] as a parameter but int params are not allowed.

data {
  int T;
  int K;  // states
  real y[T];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=-1, upper=1> phi[K];
  real<lower=0> alpha[K];
  simplex[K] state[T, K];
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  real<lower=0> sigma_s;
}
model {
  int kk;
  alpha ~ normal(mean(y), 1);
  phi ~ normal(.5, .5);
  for (i in 1:K)
    state[1, i] ~ beta(1.0 / K, 1.0);
  for (t in 2:T) {
    for (i in 1:K) {
      state[t, i] ~ normal(state[t - 1, i], sigma_s);
    }
    kk ~ categorical(to_vector(state[t, ])); // compiler fails
    y[t] ~ normal(alpha[kk] + phi[kk] * y[t - 1], sigma);
  }
}

--

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: HMM AR1
parts:
On Monday, March 27, 2017 at 8:48:36 AM UTC-4, Dirk Nachbar wrote:
I am trying to build a HMM AR(1) model with potentially more than 2 states. I am struggling with the `state` matrix. Every t-th row should be a simplex. I am obviously doing something wrong with the indexing of `state`.
You have to integrate out the states. I believe there is an example in the manual.
It would also be nice to keep kk[T] as a parameter but int params are not allowed.

The parameters block does not allow you to declare an int because NUTS requires the posterior log-kernel to be differentiable with respect to the unknowns. Declaring kk as an int inside the model block does not overcome this fundamental fact. It gets initialized to the most negative integer and so categorical() fails.

Ben
